name: Amayesh Registration (Afghan and Iraqi Nationals)

requirements.blocker_text: Re-registration in the Amayesh/Hoviat system has, in practice, only been open to Afghan and Iraqi nationals with a prior Amayesh or Hoviat card from an earlier registration exercise; children may be included only where both parents already held a valid card. This is a population-specific, largely closed re-registration system rather than a general, first-time asylum application process open to all nationalities or to new arrivals without prior registration history.

evidence_required.document: Prior Amayesh or Hoviat registration card

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: must remain within the designated registration area; travel outside it requires separate permission

sources.title: UNHCR Iran -- explains the Amayesh/Hoviat registration and card-renewal system, which in practice has served as Iran's functional equivalent of refugee status for previously-registered Afghan and Iraqi nationals, administered on an annual renewal basis via government-designated Kefalat centers since 2013

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Iran). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to UNHCR's own Iran operation page (tier 2, intergovernmental), not a fetched Iranian government BAFIA (Bureau for Aliens and Foreign Immigrants Affairs) source; a government original was not located/fetched in this build. IMPORTANT SCOPING CAVEAT, WORTH LEADING WITH RATHER THAN BURYING: unlike this dataset's other international_protection routes (built around a general domestic asylum law open to claimants of any nationality -- e.g. Kenya's Refugees Act 2021, Ghana's 1992 law, Somalia's 2023 law), Iran's Amayesh/Hoviat system is NOT a general asylum-application mechanism. It is a population-specific (Afghan and, to a lesser extent, Iraqi), largely closed re-registration system: eligibility in recent registration rounds has been restricted to those who already held an earlier Amayesh or Hoviat card, meaning this route functions mainly as a renewal mechanism for an existing registered population rather than an open first-instance route for new asylum seekers of any nationality. Iran does not appear (in the sources reviewed in this build) to have a codified, general domestic asylum law comparable to those modeled elsewhere in this dataset -- the closest functional equivalent is this administrative, population-specific card system. UNHCR itself is present and operating in Iran (unlike Tunisia, where its mandate has been suspended by the government since June 2024) and continues to describe Amayesh as translating, in practice, to refugee status for its registered population, though it remains formally a renewable administrative documentation system rather than a status granted under asylum law. work_rights and study_rights set 'restricted' since the source describes access to employment and education 'within specified fields' rather than unrestricted access; family_can_work left null since dependents' specific work rights were not detailed.
